title: Orthogonal spectral norm on the fraction field of a finite affinoid domain
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_e\rangle$, $e\ge0$, be the restricted-series Tate algebra [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with Gauss norm $G$. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ with absolute value $|a/b|_F=G(a)/G(b)$. Let $C\ne0$ be an affinoid integral domain over $K$, that is, an integral domain which is a quotient of a finite-variable restricted-series algebra $K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_m\rangle$ [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], and let $j:T\hookrightarrow C$ an injective $K$-algebra homomorphism making $C$ a finitely generated $T$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, viewed as an extension of $F$. Then $[L:F]=n<\infty$. There is a nonarchimedean $F$-vector-space norm $N$ on $L$, satisfying $N(fz)=|f|_F N(z)$, whose restriction to $C$ is $\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}C}|c\bmod\mathfrak m|$ [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. There is an $F$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $L$ such that $N(\sum_{k=1}^n f_kv_k)=\max_{1\le k\le n}|f_k|_F N(v_k)$ for every $f_k\in F$. Moreover, one such $N$, for which all of the preceding properties hold simultaneously, is given explicitly: for $z\in L$ with monic minimal polynomial $Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iZ^{r-i}\in F[Z]$, $N(z)=\max_{1\le i\le r}|a_i|_F^{1/i}$. The extension $L/F$ need not be separable, and $N$ is not asserted to be multiplicative.

source.place: Section 5.3.2, Stability Theorem 1, with Section 3.8.1, Proposition 7, as applied in the domain case of the proof of Theorem 6.4.1/3, printed pp.251–252. Algebraically closed K is stable. This is the cartesian fraction-field input, before the Tate-module finiteness argument. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], every $b\in C$ is integral over $T$. For $b\ne0$ choose a monic relation of least degree $b^r+t_1b^{r-1}+\cdots+t_r=0$. Its constant term is nonzero: otherwise division by $b$ in the domain gives a shorter relation. Thus $b^{-1}=-(b^{r-1}+t_1b^{r-2}+\cdots+t_{r-1})/t_r$. Every fraction in $L$ consequently has denominator in $T\setminus\{0\}$. A finite $T$-generating list of $C$ therefore spans $L$ over $F$, so $n=[L:F]<\infty$ (and $n\ge1$).

source.place: BGR 6.4.1/3, domain case, printed pp.251-252 (scan PDF pp.257-258); 3.6.1/1 and 5.3.2/1. Primary scan read 2026-10-24.

proof.text: $K$ is stable by [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]: every finite extension is $K$ itself since $K$ is algebraically closed, and the basis $(1)$ has the stated equality, its minimal polynomials being $Z-a$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-gauss-fraction-stability] to obtain the asserted Gauss absolute value on $F$ and stability of $F$.

source.place: BGR 6.4.1/3, domain case, printed pp.251-252 (scan PDF pp.257-258); 3.6.1/1 and 5.3.2/1. Primary scan read 2026-10-24.

proof.text: Define $N=s_{L/F}$ by the displayed minimal-polynomial formula. Step 1 makes $L/F$ algebraic, so [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] gives definiteness, the strong triangle inequality and $N(fz)=|f|_FN(z)$. Stability of $F$, unfolded using [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field], supplies an $F$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $N(\sum f_kv_k)=\max_k|f_k|_FN(v_k)$.

source.place: BGR 6.4.1/3, domain case, printed pp.251-252 (scan PDF pp.257-258); 3.6.1/1 and 5.3.2/1. Primary scan read 2026-10-24.

proof.text: Fix $c\in C$. It is $T$-torsion-free because $j$ is injective and $C$ is a domain. By [lem-trf-tate-torsionfree-fibre-polynomial], the evaluation kernel in $T[Z]$ is generated by a monic $p_c=Z^r+\sum t_iZ^{r-i}$. This is also the minimal polynomial over $F$: if $h\in F[Z]$ vanishes at $c$, clear its finitely many denominators to get $dh\in T[Z]$; then $dh=p_cq$, hence $h=p_c(q/d)$ in $F[Z]$. Thus $N(c)=\max_iG(t_i)^{1/i}$.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, Section 1.4, Lemma 12(i)-(iii), printed pp.25-27; primary text read 2026-10-24.

proof.text: For each $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}T$, the same fibre-polynomial lemma gives a nonempty fibre and $\max_{\mathfrak n\mid\mathfrak m}|c\bmod\mathfrak n|=\max_i|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/i}$. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$ lies over a maximal ideal of $T$: its residue field is finite over $K$ by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], so the image of $T$ there is a finite-dimensional $K$-domain, hence a field. Taking suprema over these fibres and commuting a finite maximum and the increasing continuous positive roots gives $\rho_C(c)=\max_i\rho_T(t_i)^{1/i}=\max_iG(t_i)^{1/i}=N(c)$. Here $\rho_T=G$ is exactly the Tate clause of that calculus node. This proves the restriction for the same $N$ as in step 3, including $c=0$.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, Section 1.4, Lemma 12(i)-(iii), printed pp.25-27; primary text read 2026-10-24.
